questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Uganda is located on which continent?
questions.explanation: Uganda is a country in East Africa, which is part of the African continent.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country lies to the east of Uganda?
questions.explanation: Kenya borders Uganda on the eastern side.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country borders Uganda to the west?
questions.explanation: The Democratic Republic of Congo lies to the west of Uganda.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country is found to the north of Uganda?
questions.explanation: South Sudan borders Uganda in the north.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country borders Uganda to the south-west?
questions.explanation: Rwanda lies to the south-west of Uganda.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country lies to the south of Uganda?
questions.explanation: Tanzania borders Uganda on the south.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is the capital city of Uganda?
questions.explanation: Kampala is the capital and largest city of Uganda.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which large lake occupies part of Uganda's southern border?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria lies along Uganda's southern border and is shared with Kenya and Tanzania.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which river forms part of Uganda's border with the Democratic Republic of Congo?
questions.explanation: The River Semliki flows between Lake Edward and Lake Albert and forms part of the border with the D.R. Congo.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is the longest river flowing through Uganda?
questions.explanation: The River Nile is the longest river flowing through Uganda.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The source of the River Nile in Uganda is associated with which lake?
questions.explanation: The Nile leaves Lake Victoria at Jinja and flows northwards.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which physical feature is found in eastern Uganda?
questions.explanation: Mount Elgon rises in eastern Uganda on the border with Kenya.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The Rwenzori Mountains are mainly found in which part of Uganda?
questions.explanation: The Rwenzori Mountains lie in western Uganda.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which mountain is associated with the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo?
questions.explanation: The Rwenzori Mountains lie along the Uganda–D.R. Congo border.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why are mountains important to people?
options: B. They provide areas for farming and tourism
C. They stop rivers from flowing
questions.explanation: Mountain slopes often have fertile soils and attract tourists, so they support farming and tourism.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which physical feature is a low-lying area between hills or mountains?
questions.explanation: A valley is the low ground lying between higher land.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which physical feature is generally higher than the surrounding land and has a relatively flat top?
questions.explanation: A plateau is raised land with a fairly flat surface on top.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is a drainage feature?
questions.explanation: Drainage features are water features such as rivers, lakes and swamps.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why are rivers important to farmers?
questions.explanation: Rivers supply water for crops, animals and irrigation.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which activity can be carried out on some lakes and rivers?
questions.explanation: Lakes and rivers support fishing, transport and water supply.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is climate?
options: A. The condition of the atmosphere at a particular moment
B. The average weather conditions of an area over a long period
C. The amount of soil in an area
D. The shape of the land
questions.explanation: Weather is what happens on one day; climate is the average over many years.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure rainfall?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge collects rain so the amount can be measured.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which instrument measures temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the air is.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which factor is likely to affect the amount of rainfall received in an area?
questions.explanation: Relief matters because air forced to rise over highlands cools and drops rain.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is rainfall important to farmers?
options: A. It provides water for crops
B. It removes all fertile soil
questions.explanation: Crops need water, and most Ugandan farming depends on rainfall.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is vegetation?
options: A. Animals found in an area
B. Plants growing naturally in an area
C. People living in an area
questions.explanation: Vegetation means the plant cover growing naturally in an area.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which human activity can destroy natural vegetation?
questions.explanation: Deforestation removes trees and destroys the natural plant cover.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which practice helps conserve forests?
questions.explanation: Afforestation means planting trees, which restores and protects forest cover.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why are forests important?
options: A. They help protect the environment
questions.explanation: Forests hold soil, attract rain, give timber and shelter wildlife.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is deforestation?
options: B. Cutting down trees on a large scale
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the large-scale clearing of trees.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which soil type is generally suitable for growing many crops because it contains a mixture of soil particles?
questions.explanation: Loam mixes sand, silt and clay, so it holds both water and plant food.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which farming practice helps reduce soil erosion on sloping land?
questions.explanation: Ploughing along the contour slows water running down the slope.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is soil erosion?
options: B. Removal of the top fertile layer of soil
D. Addition of manure to soil
questions.explanation: Soil erosion is the wearing away of the fertile top layer by water or wind.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following can cause soil erosion?
questions.explanation: Removing trees leaves soil bare, so rain washes it away.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is terracing mainly used for?
options: A. Controlling soil erosion on slopes
questions.explanation: Terraces are steps cut across a slope that slow running water.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which agricultural practice involves covering the soil with plant materials?
questions.explanation: Mulching covers soil with dry grass or leaves.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: One advantage of mulching is that it:
questions.explanation: A mulch cover reduces evaporation, so the soil stays moist for longer.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is a cash crop commonly grown in Uganda?
questions.explanation: Coffee is one of Uganda's leading cash crops.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is mainly a food crop?
questions.explanation: Cassava is grown mainly to be eaten; coffee, tea and cotton are cash crops.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is agriculture important to Uganda?
options: A. It provides food and employment
C. It stops industries from operating
questions.explanation: Most Ugandans depend on farming for food, income and jobs.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which activity involves keeping animals for products such as milk and meat?
questions.explanation: Livestock farming is the rearing of animals such as cattle and goats.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which livestock product is used to make leather?
questions.explanation: Hides and skins are tanned to make leather.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which activity involves catching fish from lakes and rivers?
questions.explanation: Fishing is the catching of fish from water bodies.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which practice can help conserve fish stocks?
questions.explanation: Rules on net sizes and closed seasons let young fish grow and breed.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is a mineral resource?
questions.explanation: Copper is a mineral dug from the ground; the others are crops.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is population?
options: A. The number of people living in an area
B. The number of animals in a forest
C. The amount of rainfall received
D. The size of a lake
questions.explanation: Population means the number of people living in a place.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is a population census?
options: B. An official counting of people in a country
questions.explanation: A census is the official counting of all people in a country.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why does a government carry out a population census?
options: A. To obtain information for planning
B. To stop people from farming
questions.explanation: Census figures show how many schools, hospitals and roads are needed.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is a social service?
questions.explanation: Education, health and water supply are social services provided to people.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: One possible disadvantage of a rapidly increasing population is:
options: A. Increased pressure on social services
questions.explanation: More people need more schools, hospitals and housing than are available.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is migration?
options: A. Movement of people from one place to another
questions.explanation: Migration is the movement of people from one place to settle in another.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A person who moves from one country to another to live there is called a:
questions.explanation: A migrant is a person who moves to live in another place or country.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which factor may cause people to migrate?
options: B. Availability of nothing to do
C. Desire to avoid all services
questions.explanation: People often move to where they can find work and a better living.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is urbanisation?
options: A. Growth and expansion of towns and cities
B. Movement from towns to forests only
C. Growth of villages into forests
questions.explanation: Urbanisation is the growth of towns and cities as more people settle in them.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which settlement is more likely to have many industries and large commercial centres?
questions.explanation: Towns and cities concentrate industries, shops and services.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which means of transport is most suitable for moving bulky goods over long distances by land?
questions.explanation: Lorries on roads can carry heavy loads far inland.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which transport uses railway lines?
questions.explanation: Trains run on railway lines.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which means of transport is generally the fastest for long-distance international travel?
questions.explanation: Aircraft cover long distances far faster than any land or water transport.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is one advantage of water transport?
options: A. It can carry bulky goods
C. It can travel on mountains
D. It is always faster than aircraft
questions.explanation: Ships and ferries carry heavy, bulky cargo cheaply.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which means of communication can send information electronically over long distances?
questions.explanation: A telephone carries messages electronically over long distances.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of mass communication?
questions.explanation: Radio reaches very many people at the same time.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is communication important in economic development?
options: A. It helps people exchange information
questions.explanation: Traders, farmers and government need information to make good decisions.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is trade?
options: A. Buying and selling goods and services
questions.explanation: Trade is the exchange of goods and services, usually for money.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Trade carried out within a country is called:
questions.explanation: Internal trade takes place inside the borders of one country.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Trade between two or more countries is called:
questions.explanation: International trade crosses national borders.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is an export?
options: A. A good brought into a country
B. A good sent out of a country for sale
C. A good destroyed in a country
D. A product stored at home
questions.explanation: Exports are goods sold to other countries.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is an import?
options: A. A good brought into a country for sale or use
B. A good sent out of a country
C. A crop grown at home
D. A locally made product only
questions.explanation: Imports are goods bought from other countries.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following can Uganda export?
options: D. Cars made in every country
questions.explanation: Coffee is one of Uganda's main export earners.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is industry important?
options: A. It processes raw materials into useful products
C. It destroys all raw materials
questions.explanation: Industries add value to raw materials and create jobs.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which industry processes cotton into products such as cloth?
questions.explanation: Textile industries spin and weave cotton into cloth.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is a member of the East African Community?
questions.explanation: Uganda is a member state of the East African Community.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country is found to the east of Uganda and is a member of the East African Community?
questions.explanation: Kenya lies east of Uganda and is an EAC member.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is one major purpose of regional cooperation in East Africa?
options: A. To promote cooperation among member states
C. To stop movement of all goods
questions.explanation: Regional bodies exist so neighbouring states can work together for shared benefit.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which activity can strengthen cooperation among East African countries?
questions.explanation: Trading together builds shared interests and stronger ties.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which lake is shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria borders all three countries.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which East African country is famous for Mount Kilimanjaro?
questions.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain, is in Tanzania.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country has Kigali as its capital?
questions.explanation: Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is the capital city of Kenya?
questions.explanation: Nairobi is Kenya's capital and largest city.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is the capital city of Tanzania?
questions.explanation: Dodoma is the official capital of Tanzania, although Dar es Salaam is the largest city.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is Lake Victoria important to East African countries?
options: A. It supports fishing, transport and other economic activities
D. It separates Africa from Europe
questions.explanation: The lake provides fish, water and a transport route for three countries.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Who is a citizen?
options: A. A legally recognised member of a country
B. Any tourist visiting a country
C. Any animal living in a country
questions.explanation: A citizen is a legally recognised member of a country with rights and duties.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is a responsibility of a good citizen?
questions.explanation: Good citizens obey the law and protect public property.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is a right of a child?
questions.explanation: Every child has a right to education.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why should citizens obey laws?
options: A. To promote order and peaceful living
questions.explanation: Laws keep order so people can live and work together peacefully.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is democracy?
options: A. A system in which people participate in choosing their leaders
questions.explanation: In a democracy, the people choose their leaders and take part in decisions.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is an election?
options: A. A process of choosing leaders
B. A process of building a road
C. A process of planting crops
D. A process of measuring rainfall
questions.explanation: An election is how citizens choose their leaders by voting.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why are elections important?
options: A. They allow citizens to choose representatives
C. They stop citizens from participating
questions.explanation: Elections give citizens a say in who governs them.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which arm of government makes laws?
questions.explanation: The Legislature, or Parliament, debates and passes laws.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which arm of government interprets laws?
questions.explanation: Courts under the Judiciary interpret and apply the law.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which arm of government implements laws and government policies?
questions.explanation: The Executive carries out the laws and runs the day-to-day work of government.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Who were missionaries?
options: A. People who travelled to spread their religion and provide related services
B. People who came only to trade gold
C. People who came only to hunt
D. People who built every railway in Africa
questions.explanation: Missionaries came to spread their faith and also started schools and health centres.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which group played an important role in spreading Islam in East Africa?
questions.explanation: Arab traders reaching the coast and interior spread Islam alongside their trade.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why did some European explorers travel through Africa?
options: A. To explore and obtain geographical information
questions.explanation: Explorers mapped rivers, lakes and land and reported back to Europe.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which European country colonised Uganda?
questions.explanation: Uganda was a British protectorate until independence.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What was one major aim of colonial powers in Africa?
options: A. To control territories and their resources
B. To give all Africans political power
questions.explanation: Colonial powers wanted land, raw materials and markets.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What does independence mean?
options: A. Freedom of a country to govern itself
questions.explanation: Independence is when a country governs itself instead of being ruled by another.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Uganda gained independence from Britain in:
questions.explanation: Uganda became independent on 9th October 1962.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Who became Uganda's first Prime Minister at independence?
questions.explanation: Apollo Milton Obote was Prime Minister when Uganda became independent in 1962.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is Uganda's independence important?
options: B. It ended all economic activities
questions.explanation: Independence meant Ugandans could govern themselves and make their own laws.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following best promotes national unity?
options: A. Respecting people from different communities
questions.explanation: Treating all communities with respect binds a nation together.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A learner is facing east. In which direction will the learner's left hand point?
questions.explanation: Facing east, north is on your left and south is on your right.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A learner is facing south. In which direction will the learner's right hand point?
questions.explanation: Facing south, west is on your right and east is on your left.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A village is located north of a school. In which direction is the school from the village?
questions.explanation: Directions work both ways: if the village is north of the school, the school is south of the village.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A hospital is west of a market. Where is the market in relation to the hospital?
questions.explanation: If the hospital is west of the market, then the market must be east of the hospital.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which instrument would a learner use to determine the direction of a place in the field?
questions.explanation: A compass needle points north, so it is used to find direction.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is a map scale important?
options: A. It helps the user determine actual distances
B. It shows the colour of the map
questions.explanation: A scale tells you what a distance on the map stands for on the ground.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is a human-made feature?
questions.explanation: Roads are built by people; mountains, rivers and lakes occur naturally.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is a physical feature?
questions.explanation: A river is a natural feature; railways, roads and schools are made by people.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A map shows a railway line connecting two towns. What does the railway line help the map reader understand?
options: A. The route followed by railway transport
C. The population of the towns
questions.explanation: A railway symbol shows the route trains follow between places.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why should a learner study the key before using a map?
options: A. To understand the symbols used on the map
D. To identify the map paper
questions.explanation: The key explains what each symbol on the map stands for.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is normally shown using a symbol on a map?
questions.explanation: Features such as schools, churches and bridges are drawn as symbols.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: If two places are very close together on a map, what can this suggest?
options: A. They may be close together on the ground
B. They are always in different countries
C. One must be a mountain
D. They must have different climates
questions.explanation: Distance on a map stands for real distance, so places drawn close together are usually near each other.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which direction is directly opposite to east?
questions.explanation: East and west are opposite each other on the compass.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which direction is directly opposite to north?
questions.explanation: North and south are opposite each other on the compass.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of the following is an intermediate direction?
questions.explanation: Intermediate directions lie between the cardinal points, such as north-east.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A farmer's garden is south-east of his home. In which direction should the farmer walk to reach the garden?
questions.explanation: To reach a place lying south-east of you, you walk towards the south-east.
questions.origin: Original practice question (not a UNEB past paper)

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What does a map boundary normally show?
options: A. The limit of an area

questions.question: Why should children be protected from abuse?

questions.question: Why is peace important for East African countries?

questions.question: Which activity can strengthen relationships between East African countries?
questions.explanation: Sharing music, sport and language builds understanding between neighbours.

questions.question: Why is regional integration important?

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Uganda lies between 4°N and 1°S, which means it is crossed by the ______.
questions.explanation: The Equator (0°) passes through southern Uganda.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of these features was formed by faulting?
questions.explanation: Lake Albert lies in the Rift Valley, formed when land sank between faults.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Mount Elgon and Mount Muhavura were both formed by ______ activity.
questions.explanation: They are volcanic mountains built from material thrown out of the earth.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in Uganda?
questions.explanation: Lake Bunyonyi in Kabale is the deepest lake in Uganda.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why does Kabale receive more rainfall than Moroto?
options: A. Kabale is nearer the sea
B. Kabale is higher and receives relief rainfall
questions.explanation: High land forces moist air to rise, cool and fall as relief rainfall.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why are the shores of Lake Victoria densely populated?
options: A. The climate is very cold
B. There is reliable rainfall, fishing and fertile soil
D. There is very little water
questions.explanation: Reliable rain, fish and fertile soils support many people.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What most limits crop growing in the Karamoja region?
questions.explanation: Karamoja is semi-arid, so crops often fail without irrigation.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which national park is best known for mountain gorillas?
questions.explanation: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park protects mountain gorillas.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which raw material is used by the cement factories at Hima and Tororo?
questions.explanation: Cement is made mainly from limestone.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is the River Nile at Jinja suitable for generating hydro-electric power?
options: B. It has a steady flow and a fall in the land
D. It dries up in the dry season
questions.explanation: A constant flow plus a drop in level turns turbines all year.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which problem most threatens fish stocks on Lake Victoria today?
options: B. Overfishing and use of illegal nets
C. Too many boats on land
questions.explanation: Catching immature fish with illegal nets reduces future stocks.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A person facing North turns 180° clockwise. The new direction faced is ______.
questions.explanation: A half turn of 180° from North brings you to South.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: On a map with a scale of 1:100,000, a distance of 4 cm represents ______ on the ground.
questions.explanation: 1 cm stands for 100,000 cm = 1 km, so 4 cm stands for 4 km.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Lines drawn on a map to join places of the same height are called ______.
questions.explanation: Contours show the shape and height of the land.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Contour lines drawn very close together show ______.
questions.explanation: The closer the contours, the steeper the slope.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A six-figure grid reference locates a place to the nearest ______.
questions.explanation: Four figures give 1 km; six figures narrow it to 100 m.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which element of a map tells the reader what the map is about?
questions.explanation: The title states the subject and area of the map.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A map shows many buildings, a hospital, a school and tarmac roads close together. This area is most likely ______.
questions.explanation: Dense buildings and services are signs of a town.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The first Arab trader to reach Buganda, Ahmed bin Ibrahim, arrived during the reign of Kabaka ______.
questions.explanation: Ahmed bin Ibrahim reached Buganda in 1844 during Kabaka Suna II's reign.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Captain Frederick Lugard signed a treaty with Kabaka Mwanga in the year ______.
questions.explanation: The 1890 treaty brought Buganda under the Imperial British East Africa Company.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Uganda attained her independence on 9th October ______.
questions.explanation: Uganda became independent on 9th October 1962.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which system of administration did the British mainly use in Buganda?
questions.explanation: Indirect rule governed through existing chiefs and kings.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The French governed their West African colonies using the policy of ______.
questions.explanation: Assimilation aimed to make colonial subjects adopt French culture.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Who led Ghana to independence in 1957?
questions.explanation: Kwame Nkrumah led Ghana, the first African country south of the Sahara to be independent.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The Maji Maji rebellion was fought against ______ rule in Tanganyika.
questions.explanation: The Maji Maji rebellion of 1905-1907 was against German rule.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why did many Africans resist paying colonial taxes?
options: B. Taxes were forced on them and they saw few benefits
questions.explanation: Taxes were compulsory, paid in cash, and returned little to the people.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What was the main reason for building the Uganda Railway?
options: B. To ease movement of goods and administration to the interior
questions.explanation: The railway opened the interior for trade and colonial administration.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The discovery of which material marked the end of the Stone Age?
questions.explanation: Iron tools were stronger than stone and changed farming and warfare.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The present Constitution of Uganda was promulgated in the year ______.
questions.explanation: Uganda's current Constitution was promulgated in 1995.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which arm of government interprets the law?
questions.explanation: Courts under the Judiciary interpret and apply the law.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A by-election is held when ______.
options: B. A parliamentary seat falls vacant before the next general election
D. A new district is created
questions.explanation: A by-election fills a seat left vacant between general elections.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which one is a sign of good governance?
questions.explanation: Accountability means leaders explain how they use public resources.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: On the Uganda national flag, the black colour stands for the ______ of Africa.
questions.explanation: Black stands for the people, yellow for sunshine, red for brotherhood.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Two neighbouring villages disagree over the use of a water source. What is the best way to solve this?
options: B. Dialogue and mediation by local leaders
questions.explanation: Peaceful dialogue settles disputes without harming either side.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which local council level is closest to the people in a village?
questions.explanation: LC I is the village council, the level nearest to the people.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What is the main work of the East African Legislative Assembly?
options: A. Making laws for the Community
questions.explanation: EALA debates and passes laws for the East African Community.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which one is a benefit Uganda gets from the East African Community?
options: A. A wider market for her goods
questions.explanation: A common market lets Ugandan goods sell freely across member states.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Uganda is a landlocked country. Which problem does this create?
options: B. She depends on other countries' sea ports, raising costs
questions.explanation: Goods must travel overland to Mombasa or Dar es Salaam, adding cost and delay.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The longest river in Africa is the River ______.
questions.explanation: The Nile is the longest river in Africa.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The largest desert in Africa is the ______ Desert.
questions.explanation: The Sahara stretches across northern Africa.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which African country was never colonised?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia kept her independence throughout the colonial period.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The highest mountain in Africa is Mount ______.
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is Africa's highest mountain.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: How does the vegetation of the Congo Basin differ from that of the Sahel?
options: A. The Congo Basin has dense rain forest while the Sahel has short grass and thorny scrub
C. The Congo Basin is desert
D. The Sahel has rain forest
questions.explanation: Heavy rainfall gives the Congo Basin thick forest; the dry Sahel supports only scrub.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which organisation replaced the Organisation of African Unity?
questions.explanation: The African Union replaced the OAU in 2002.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Match each person with what they are remembered for in Uganda's history.
pairs: Reported the source of the Nile
Signed the 1890 treaty with Kabaka Mwanga
First Prime Minister of independent Uganda
questions.explanation: Each figure played a different role in Uganda's history.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country borders Uganda to the north?
questions.explanation: South Sudan lies to the north of Uganda.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Uganda is described as a landlocked country because it has no ______.
questions.explanation: A landlocked country has no direct access to the sea.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of these is a man-made lake in Uganda?
questions.explanation: Uganda's named lakes here are natural; reservoirs behind dams are man-made.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is an economic use of swamps in Uganda?
options: A. Making papyrus mats and crafts
questions.explanation: Papyrus from swamps is used for mats, baskets and crafts.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which factor explains why Entebbe has a moderate climate?
options: A. It is far from water
B. The influence of Lake Victoria
questions.explanation: Large water bodies moderate nearby temperatures.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which vegetation type is found in the Karamoja region?
options: B. Dry savanna and thorn bush
questions.explanation: Low rainfall gives Karamoja dry savanna and thorn bush.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is continuous cropping without manure harmful?
options: B. It removes plant nutrients and lowers yields
questions.explanation: Crops take nutrients out; without replacement the soil is exhausted.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Population density is best described as the number of people ______.
questions.explanation: Density compares population with the area of land.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why is settlement sparse in the Kidepo area?
options: B. Wildlife protection and dry conditions
questions.explanation: Protected park land and dryness limit settlement.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which mineral is quarried for building stone and road making?
questions.explanation: Granite is quarried and crushed for construction.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which industry would most likely be set up near a large fishing landing site?
questions.explanation: Processing near the source keeps fish fresh and cuts transport cost.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is a benefit of tourism to Uganda's economy?
questions.explanation: Tourists spend foreign currency in the country.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which action best protects wildlife while still allowing tourism?
options: B. Controlled visits with trained guides
questions.explanation: Managed visits earn money without harming animals.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which practice reduces the effects of deforestation most directly?
options: A. Planting trees and using energy-saving stoves
questions.explanation: Replanting and using less fuelwood reduce forest loss.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which mode is most suitable for carrying heavy goods over long distances by land?
questions.explanation: Railways carry bulky, heavy goods cheaply over land.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is an intermediate direction?
questions.explanation: Intermediate directions lie between cardinal points.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A person facing South West turns 90° clockwise. They now face ______.
questions.explanation: From SW, a quarter turn clockwise gives NW.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A map has a scale of 1:25,000. A road measures 8 cm. Its real length is ______.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A blue line marked on a map most likely shows a ______.
questions.explanation: Blue is used for water features such as rivers.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why must a map have a key?
options: B. To explain what the symbols mean
questions.explanation: Without a key a reader cannot interpret the symbols.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: In a grid reference, which figures are read first?
questions.explanation: Read eastings (along) before northings (up).

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A river on a map bends and has many small streams joining it. These streams are called ______.
questions.explanation: Streams that join a bigger river are tributaries.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A map shows a settlement at the meeting point of three roads. This settlement most likely grew because of ______.
options: B. Its position as a route centre for trade
questions.explanation: Route centres attract trade and settlement.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Early people in Africa first got food by ______.
questions.explanation: Before farming, people hunted animals and gathered wild food.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The Bantu are believed to have entered East Africa mainly from the ______.
questions.explanation: Bantu groups are believed to have moved in from the west and south west.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which kingdom was ruled by the Bahinda dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Bahinda dynasty ruled Ankole.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which two explorers are associated with reaching Lake Victoria region in the 1860s?
questions.explanation: Speke and Grant travelled in the Lake Victoria region in the 1860s.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which of these was an effect of missionary work in Uganda?
options: A. Growth of schools and hospitals
questions.explanation: Missionaries founded many early schools and health centres.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which goods did Arab traders mainly seek in the East African interior?
questions.explanation: Ivory and slaves were the main goods sought.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Under indirect rule, the British governed mainly through ______.
options: B. Existing local chiefs and rulers
questions.explanation: Indirect rule used local rulers to administer for the British.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The Uganda Agreement of 1900 was signed between the British and ______.
questions.explanation: The 1900 Agreement was made with Buganda.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which political party led Uganda at independence in 1962?
questions.explanation: The Uganda People's Congress led the government at independence.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: What was the main aim of African nationalist movements?
options: B. To win self-rule and independence
questions.explanation: Nationalists campaigned for their countries to govern themselves.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why did the first East African Community collapse in 1977?
options: B. Political differences and mistrust among members
questions.explanation: Political disagreements between the three states broke it up.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A person who becomes a citizen of Uganda after living there for the required period gains citizenship by ______.
questions.explanation: Long residence can lead to citizenship by registration or naturalisation.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is a fundamental human right?
options: B. The right to break laws
C. The right to avoid taxes
D. The right to damage property
questions.explanation: The right to life is a basic human right.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is a duty of a citizen towards the environment?
options: A. Protecting forests and water sources
questions.explanation: Citizens must protect the environment for everyone.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which practice best shows democracy at work?
questions.explanation: Democracy lets people choose leaders in free, fair elections.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The rule of law means ______.
options: A. Leaders are above the law
B. Everyone, including leaders, obeys the law
D. Laws apply to the poor only
questions.explanation: Under the rule of law nobody is above the law.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The constitution of a country is best described as ______.
options: B. The supreme law that guides how a country is governed
questions.explanation: A constitution is the supreme law of the land.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which body makes by-laws for a district?
questions.explanation: District councils pass by-laws for their areas.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which body organises national elections in Uganda?
questions.explanation: The Electoral Commission organises and supervises elections.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which action best promotes national unity?
questions.explanation: Equal treatment builds trust and unity.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Two groups disagree over grazing land. Which approach is most likely to bring lasting peace?
options: B. Negotiation and a shared agreement
questions.explanation: Agreements reached together tend to last.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which national symbol is played or sung at official ceremonies?
questions.explanation: The National Anthem is sung at official events.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The capital city of Rwanda is ______.
questions.explanation: Kigali is Rwanda's capital city.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which activity is most important along the East African coast?
questions.explanation: Coastal areas depend on fishing and tourism.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why does Uganda pay more for imported goods than Kenya does?
options: B. Goods must travel far inland from the sea port
questions.explanation: Inland transport from Mombasa adds cost.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: A common market among neighbouring countries mainly helps by ______.
options: A. Widening the market for goods
questions.explanation: A common market lets goods sell across all member states.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which is the largest country in Africa by area?
questions.explanation: Algeria is Africa's largest country by area.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: The Atlas Mountains are found in ______ Africa.
questions.explanation: The Atlas Mountains lie in north west Africa.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why does the Sahel suffer frequent droughts?
options: A. It is near the sea
B. It receives low and unreliable rainfall
questions.explanation: The Sahel borders the desert and gets little, unreliable rain.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Which country is a leading producer of cocoa in West Africa?
questions.explanation: Ghana is a major cocoa producer.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Why are river valleys such as the Nile Valley densely populated?
options: A. Water for farming and settlement
questions.explanation: Reliable water supports farming and dense settlement.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Most African countries gained independence during which period?
questions.explanation: The wave of African independence came in the 1950s and 1960s.

questions.subject: SST
questions.question: Match each arm of government with its main work.
questions.explanation: Each body has a separate role, which prevents abuse of power.
